title: Account Mappings lists one row per category under Parts cost of goods sold
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Under "Parts cost of goods sold" rows show named "Internal: General Internal", "No Charge: Warranty", "No Charge: Goodwill" and "No Charge: Comeback".
  • Each row is a picker over the organization's chart of accounts, like the other rows.
  • The existing "Shop supplies expense" row is still there and no new shop supplies row was added.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11763 (Story 6, AccountingHub account mapping), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S6-R1: “Accounting > Account Mappings shows one row per category under "Parts cost of goods sold", named after the category ("Internal: General Internal", "No Charge: Warranty"), each a picker over the organization's chart of accounts like the other rows. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row and can still be remapped, so a held entry of that category can post. The shop supplies amount of Story 10 is credited to the existing "Shop supplies expense" row; no new row for it. An empty row holds the event (S8-N2); there is no fallback to another row. Same model as S5-R6: the row lives on the category, archiving keeps it, Restore brings it back.”
  • S10-R5: “No new mapping row in either integration: QuickBooks credits the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) (Story 5, S5-R1 note); AccountingHub uses its existing "Shop supplies expense" row (Story 6).”
